about.summary:
This is the documentation home of the **HippoCampusRobotics** lab at TUHH's Institute of
Mechanics and Ocean Engineering. It brings four things into one place: setup guides
(migrated page for page from the old Sphinx sit

index:home.summary: The lab's home for getting robots running: setup guides, every project in one place, searchable code and CAD, and the tools our AI agents use.

index:projects.summary: Everything the lab builds, grouped into projects. One project can own many repositories; forks of upstream software are listed inside the project that uses them.

index:tools.summary: MCP servers are small programs that give AI agents real capabilities — renting a GPU, reading a CAD assembly — through a standard interface. These are the lab's tools. Each page will take you from nothing installed to a working agent connection.

projects/acoustics.summary:
Acoustic sensing around the vehicles: the doppler velocity log (DVL) that measures
velocity over ground, and the message definitions for acoustic ranging and modems.

projects/cameras.summary:
Image streams into ROS: the MJPEG USB camera driver the vehicles use, and the event-camera
work from a research collaboration.

projects/core-stack.summary:
The shared ROS 2 software every lab vehicle runs: control, state estimation, the message
definitions that tie nodes together, and the meta packages that pull a full system onto a
robot. If you contribute code to the lab,

projects/dev-infrastructure.summary:
How software actually reaches robots and users: deployment configuration for onboard
computers, the bot that builds Debian packages, and the dependency definitions that make
`rosdep` work for lab packages.

projects/docs-and-site.summary:
The lab's documentation about itself: the current Sphinx docs site, the org website, and
the org profile.

projects/hippocampus-vehicle.summary:
The HippoCampus is the lab's own micro autonomous underwater vehicle: a small torpedo-shaped
robot sized for the institute's tank. This project collects everything that defines the
physical vehicle — the CAD model, the P

projects/holiday-fun.summary:
`hippo-christmas` — festive hardware humor from 2022, preserved because labs that keep
their jokes keep their people.

projects/lab-infrastructure.summary:
The systems around the water that every experiment leans on: Qualisys motion capture for
millimeter ground truth, the gantry that moves equipment over the tank, and the physical
button boxes wired into the safety and con

projects/legacy-ros1.summary:
The pre-ROS 2 HippoCampus software stack, preserved. The lab moved to ROS 2; these repos
stay readable for anyone revisiting old experiments or wondering why something is shaped
the way it is.

projects/localization.summary:
Knowing where the vehicle is inside the tank. The current approach is visual: cameras on
the vehicle detect AprilTag markers, and an EKF fuses the detections into a pose estimate.
Earlier acoustic and radio-frequency app

projects/radio-comms.summary:
Getting data to and from vehicles without a tether: the HippoLink telemetry link over
Si1000-family radios, the MAVLink plumbing underneath, and software-defined radio
experiments.

projects/scalar-field.summary:
Informative path planning over scalar fields — temperature-like quantities spread over the
tank. The vehicle maintains a belief about the field and plans where measuring next helps
most. This is the lab's active research

projects/simulation.summary:
Run the robots in software before the tank: Gazebo worlds, the plugins that make water
behave like water (buoyancy, drag, thrusters), and the vehicle models.

projects/teaching.summary:
The lab's teaching side: the **Formulas and Vehicles** course, where students program
underwater robots, and the Python onramp that gets them ready.

projects/uvms.summary:
An underwater vehicle-manipulator system: a BlueROV2 Heavy carrying a Reach Robotics
Alpha 5 arm, with an end-effector trajectory-tracking framework — the vehicle and the arm
move together so the gripper follows a comman
